candidate_changes.note: Full Python regression passed locally on locked dependencies (341 passed, 1 skipped, 68% statement coverage). Yosys-backed LEC/formal/synth fixtures pass on the FIFO example and dedicated RTL fixtures; synthesis output is a technology-independent gate netlist, not a vendor mapping or bitstream. The SystemVerilog support matrix is measured per tool (docs/systemverilog.md) and Icarus/Yosys have documented limits on interfaces, package ports, classes and import. The class-based environment (docs/svsim.md) is a small self-authored transaction/driver/scoreboard set, not a UVM library, and reports blocked when Verilator/C++/make are unavailable. Stage 2 adds a vendor-neutral implementation layer (docs/backends.md): the open iCE40 backend produces a real .bin bitstream through Yosys synth_ice40 -> nextpnr-ice40 -> icepack, the anlogic backend is a thin adapter over the existing TD flow, and the generic backend honestly reports synthesis-only with no place-and-route or bitstream. Stage 3 closes the verification loop on the RTL itself: icforge coverage builds and runs a self-checking testbench with Verilator --binary --coverage and parses the SystemC coverage.dat into per-source line/branch/toggle/expr structural coverage (docs/coverage.md), reported through the optional COV-001 gate; structural coverage is not functional or assertion coverage and does not claim all behavior was exercised. Stage 4 adds a source-level CDC/RDC structural heuristic (docs/cdc.md): icforge cdc splits processes by always/initial, extracts clock and reset domains, and flags signals driven in one domain and read in a disjoint one as candidates; it does not prove CDC safety, does not expand generate/netlist, and treats reset-domain hints as review items (CDC-001 optional gate; cdc_dual_clk fixture measured review_required). Stage 5 adds functional coverage on the same pipeline (docs/coverage.md): icforge coverage --functional-coverage collects cover property points (Verilator user coverage points) and treats a fired concurrent assert property as a hard fail (COV-002 optional gate, separate from COV-001); the functional_cov fixture measured 20/20 structural + 4/4 functional points with no assertion failure, and the testbench uses a reset-based assertion because Verilator samples clock-edge assertions post-NBA. Stage 6 adds the post-route timing/physical-signoff path (docs/timing.md): icforge timing summarizes the real static timing signoff recorded by nextpnr-ice40 in reports/implement.json (ice40_pwm measured PASS at 326.9 MHz vs 12.0 MHz constraint) and reports post_route_status=blocked because icesim is not available in this environment (TIM-001 optional gate); it does not fabricate post-route simulation or claim ASIC physical signoff (DV-004 still not_run). Stage 7 adds versioned release aggregation (docs/release.md): icforge release runs the full review, writes reports/release.json with the aggregate verdict and every gate status, and hands off to package with a version suffix (delivery.json carries release_version); engineering_signoff remains not_granted. Vendor-neutral delivery is now wired in: DELIV-001 records delivery evidence for a non-Anlogic bitstream-capable target, artifact_ready accepts either the Anlogic TD path or an open-backend bitstream, and package writes the .bin plus delivery.json vendor_neutral_bitstream. The iCE40 bitstream remains real but unprogrammed and not board-verified; iCE40 post-route simulation (icesim) is unavailable in this environment (no yowasp-icesim package) and is explicitly not claimed. Per-project CPU/video application is not yet done. RSI roadmap stage 4 adds the tiny_gpu fixture (examples/agent_validation/tiny_gpu): a lockstep SIMT core with 4 lanes, a PTX-like instruction subset (movi/mov/add/sub/mul/mad/ld/st/setp.lt/bra/exit), per-lane register file and data bank, and a 4-element dot-product MAC kernel. It passes icforge verify (7 REQ checks incl. 32-bit wraparound reference model), lint, synth (40938 cells/4978 flops), coverage (3158/3158 RTL points 100%), and cdc (no crossings). icforge lec times out at 300s on this multiplier-dense netlist (WASM Yosys SAT budget), a documented scaling limit; LEC is not claimed for this fixture. The fixture is a minimum inference-only SIMT engine, not a CUDA-compatible GPU: no PTX assembler, no CUDA runtime, no warp scheduler, no divergent control flow. RSI roadmap stage 5 adds the tiny_lpu fixture (examples/agent_validation/tiny_lpu): a tensor streaming processor with on-chip weight SRAM (4 banks x 16 words), a streaming activation input, a parallel MAC array, deterministic lockstep execution, and a streaming-complete done signal. It passes icforge verify (7 REQ checks incl. 32-bit wraparound reference model, second-streaming run, and paused/resumed partial stream), lint, synth (17411 cells/2186 flops), coverage (720/720 RTL points 100%), and cdc (no crossings). It is a single-layer GEMV engine, not a multi-layer transformer inference system: no sparse tensors, no mixed precision, no on-chip interconnect, no open-model end-to-end run. RSI roadmap stage 6 adds the tiny_train_gpu fixture (examples/agent_validation/tiny_train_gpu): the forward-pass compute core of a training GPU, with on-chip A/B/C SRAM, host load/read ports, a triple-nested integer GEMM (C = ReLU(A*B)) with a raw no-ReLU bypass, and a deterministic N^3-cycle loop. It passes icforge verify (7 REQ checks incl. 32-bit wraparound reference model, raw mode, second run, reset clears C), lint, synth (6907 cells/1576 flops), coverage (701/701 RTL points 100%), and cdc (no crossings). It is a single-tile integer GEMM, not a datacenter training GPU: no large matrix array, no high-bandwidth memory, no FP8/BF16 mixed precision, no interconnect. The host-side self-training loop (fpga_agent/training.py, CLI `icforge training`) trains a tiny ReLU linear model with SGD, quantizes the weights to int32, and verifies the forward pass with the same 32-bit wraparound GEMM + sign-bit ReLU math the RTL implements (default run: loss 0.282 -> 0.033, 100% forward match). This is a toy SGD loop, not a PyTorch-class training stack, and the loop is semantically aligned, not board-executed. RSI roadmap stage 7 adds the tiny_soc fixture (examples/agent_validation/tiny_soc): a minimal SoC-level integration with a memory-mapped host bus (wb_we/wb_re/wb_addr/wb_wdata/wb_rdata), an address decoder, an on-chip integer GEMM accelerator (C = ReLU(A*B), 32-bit wraparound) with A/B/C SRAM, and an 8N1 UART transmitter (BAUD_DIV cycles/bit, start/8 data LSB-first/stop). It passes icforge verify (7 REQ checks incl. 32-bit wraparound reference model and per-cycle UART capture/decode), lint, synth (8565 cells/1593 flops), coverage (716/716 RTL points 100%), and cdc (no crossings). It is a single-clock single-domain SoC tile, not a semiconductor-level architecture redesign: no CPU core, AXI/NoC, MMU, DMA, multi-clock domains, power management, or SerDes/DDR PHY. See ROADMAP.md for the full 7-stage mapping.
